prompt: Match each setting to the reader it is for.
What does Android use to decide that a package is an update and not a downgrade?

choices.text: The versionName, compared as numbers
choices.why: The name is never compared; it can be any text.

choices.text: The date the APK was built
choices.why: Dates play no part.

choices.text: The versionCode
choices.why: Right. That alone.

choices.text: Which track it came from in Google Play
choices.why: The phone does not know about tracks.

prompt: In an Expo app, where is the Android version code set?

choices.text: In expo.android.versionCode in app.json
choices.why: Right. And ios.buildNumber for iOS.

choices.text: In expo.version, the number shown on the store page
choices.why: That is the name people read.

choices.text: In the store listing
choices.why: The listing does not carry it.

choices.text: In the version field of package.json, beside the dependencies
choices.why: That is the npm package's, not the app's.

prompt: What is the largest versionCode Google Play allows?
Apple compares build numbers 9 and 10 for the same version. Which is newer?

choices.text: Whichever was uploaded last
choices.why: Upload order does not decide it.

choices.text: 9, because text sorting puts it after 10
choices.why: That is how text sorts; Apple compares numbers.

choices.text: Neither: build numbers are not ordered
choices.why: They are ordered as integers.
Right. They are compared as integers.

prompt: After 1.5.0 shipped, the team builds 1.4.1 to fix a bug for customers who stayed on 1.4. What happens on Google Play?

choices.text: It is offered only to the people on 1.4
choices.why: Play has no such targeting by installed version.

choices.text: Production refuses it; the fix has to ship as 1.5.1
choices.why: Right. One line of versions, moving forward.

choices.text: It replaces 1.5.0 for everybody
choices.why: A lower code cannot replace a higher one.

choices.text: It is accepted, since 1.4.1 was never uploaded
choices.why: Never used is not enough; it must also be higher.

prompt: Which of these does the App Store require? Choose every one.

choices.text: The version string increases from one App Store version to the next
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A build number unique among the builds of a version
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A build number equal to Android's versionCode
choices.why: Using the same is a convenience, not a rule.

choices.text: A version string of exactly three numbers
choices.why: Up to three.

prompt: Using the planner's rule, what versionCode does 2.3.4 build 7 get?
Why does `version.ts` refuse a patch of 100?

choices.text: Google Play forbids patch numbers above 99
choices.why: The limit is the rule's, not Google's.

choices.text: It would collide with 1.6.0
choices.why: Right. It would spill into the minor digits: two digits per part, or the order breaks.

choices.text: Semantic versioning ends at 99
choices.why: It has no such end.

choices.text: The code would go over 2,100,000,000
choices.why: 1.5.100 is far below that.

prompt: Where should the build counter in a real pipeline come from?

choices.text: A developer types it before each release
choices.why: That is the hand-typed code the rule exists to avoid.

choices.text: The current time in seconds
choices.why: It would overflow the two digits at once.

choices.text: A random number, checked against history
choices.why: Random breaks the order inside a version.

choices.text: The pipeline's own run number
choices.why: Right. Every run already has one.

prompt: In Fastlane, the action that raises the iOS build number is called ___.
Which release note is most useful to a person deciding whether to update?

choices.text: Sessions now sync between phone and tablet
choices.why: Right. What changed, for the reader.

choices.text: Refactored the sync engine and the database layer underneath it
choices.why: That is about the code, not the person.

choices.text: Bug fixes and performance improvements
choices.why: The most common note, and it says nothing.

choices.text: Version 1.5.0
choices.why: The number is already on the page.

prompt: A support e-mail says "it crashes on 1.5.0". What makes that sentence useful to the team?

choices.text: A version name in semantic form
choices.why: Any unique name would do.

choices.text: Nothing; only the version code helps
choices.why: The name is enough if it is unique.

choices.text: Each name maps to exactly one build
choices.why: Right. And the crash reports group by the same name.

choices.text: The store page shows the same number
choices.why: That helps the person, not the diagnosis.

prompt: Where does the lesson suggest the app show its own version and build?

choices.text: An About screen or the foot of Settings
choices.why: Right. Findable for a support conversation.

choices.text: In every push notification
choices.why: Notifications are for the person's task.

choices.text: On a splash screen at every launch
choices.why: Nobody needs it at every launch.

choices.text: Only in the store listing, where the person downloaded it
choices.why: The person may not know which version they have installed.

prompt: `version.ts 1.5.0 2` was refused. What does the history say about it?

choices.text: That 1.5.0 was never released

choices.text: That build 2 is lower than build 3

choices.text: That the name is malformed
